items: Research Your State Law: Search "[Your State] security deposit statute" to find the specific state code section that governs your deposit rights and obligations. (24 words)
Find Your Deposit Cap: Locate your state's maximum deposit limit to determine if you overpaid and what amount your landlord must return regardless of any written agreement. (26 words)
Note the Return Deadline: Find your state's deposit return timeline in the statute so you know exactly when your landlord must return your money after move-out. (25 words)
Check the Penalty Clause: Review your state's penalty provisions to understand how much your landlord automatically owes if they fail to return your deposit on time. (25 words)
Collect Payment Records: Pull bank statements, Venmo, PayPal, or Zelle records that show the exact amount you transferred to your landlord for the security deposit. (25 words)
Preserve All Correspondence: Save every text message and email exchanged with your landlord that references the deposit, unit, or move-in date as evidence of the implied contract. (26 words)
Document Move-In Condition: Create a written record of the unit's condition when you moved in, including photos and descriptions, to establish the baseline for move-out comparisons. (26 words)
Get Move-Out Inspection: Request a written move-out inspection from your landlord and keep a copy of any inspection report or checklist they provide, no matter how brief. (26 words)
Send a Demand Letter: Write to your landlord requesting your deposit back with a specific deadline, referencing your state's statute and the penalties they face for non-compliance. (26 words)
Send via Certified Mail: Mail your demand letter by certified mail with return receipt requested so you have legal proof your landlord received and ignored your request. (25 words)
File in Small Claims Court: If your landlord ignores the demand letter deadline, file a claim in your local small claims court for the deposit plus statutory penalties. (25 words)
Request Maximum Damages: When filing your claim, request the full statutory penalty amount from your state statute, not just your original deposit, because penalties apply automatically. (26 words)
